narrative: Material PL1__ME953731 exhibits smooth, near-normally distributed daily demand averaging 2,135 units with low coefficient of variation (0.13) over 216 working days. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.65, mean 1.3 days) with a bimodal distribution driven primarily by transport variability. The (r,Q) EOQ-based policy is selected to balance ordering and holding costs; safety stock of 3,031 units is required to achieve the 95% service level given the combined demand and lead time uncertainty. The order quantity of 13,146 units (above MOQ 3,377) reduces ordering frequency from ~158 to ~41 orders per year, yielding a ~40.7% total cost reduction while remaining within the 25,869-unit storage constraint.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth, high-frequency demand with continuous consumption makes a continuous-review (r,Q) model appropriate. The low demand CV (0.13) supports EOQ as the cost-minimising order quantity formula, and safety stock is sized using the combined lead time demand variance formula to cover the 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Order quantity (13,146) plus safety stock (3,031) totals 16,177 units, which is 62.5% of the 25,869-unit storage cap — no capacity constraint binds. If safety stock is raised or demand increases, monitor the remaining 9,692-unit headroom.
